newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Jan 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Jan 16.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Thursday's edition of The Wall Street Journal:
- General Motors directors are expected to approve sale of Hughes electronics' defense operations to Raytheon for about $9.5 billion on Thursday.
- Columbia/HCA Healthcare said it signed a definitive agreement to acquire Value Health.
- Apple said that because of weak quarterly sales and a resulting $120 million loss, it now expects to return to profit in the quarter ending in September, six months later than planned.
- AMR said it posted record quarterly earnings because of strong American Airlines traffic and the sale of 18 percent of its Sabre Group.
- More stocks are being traded based not on published earnings estimates, but on the "whisper" earnings that swirl among traders.
- Business inventories edged up 0.1 percent in November.
- BankAmerica and First Chicago were among big banks reporting quarterly earnings that met or exceeded expectations.
- Sun Microsystems profit rose 41 percent in the quarter as the computer maker used growth at the top of its product line to offset threats at the low end.
- Mark Whitacre was charged by a federal grand jury with defrauding Archer Daniels Midland of more than $9 million.
- DuPont didn't have to pay standard benefits to a contract worker, a federal appeals court ruled.
- Stocks fell on profit-taking after four consecutive record-setting sessions.
- Morgan Stanley is expected to name Joseph Perella head of its powerful investment banking group as part of a reorganization that could be announced as early as Thursday.
- A long-time Tandy director quit the board, saying he was penalized for criticizing the chief executive officer's performance.
- Ted Turner said he made a deal for some of Time Warner's Warner Bros movies to debut on Turner's basic cable networks.
- Sierra Health's proposed purchase of Physician Corp hit a snag over questions about a 1991 misdemeanor conviction of Sierra's CEO.
- Ahmanson posted better-than-expected quarterly profit on higher interest margins and cost-cutting moves.
- U.S. West Capital Funding Inc, a unit of U.S. West Inc, officially started marketing a five-part debt offering totaling $3.5 billion.
